title: Prepositional phrases
subtitle: by mistake, on purpose, in a hurry
summary: Learn fixed phrases built from by, on, in or at + a noun, and tell apart pairs like on time and in time.

lesson.heading: by + noun
lesson.text: **By** + noun often tells you how something happened. Note that there is no *the* or *a* in these phrases.

examples.note: = I thought it was my pen
= it wasn't planned; it was luck
= he did not want or plan to do it

left.label: by accident
left.text: The person did not plan it and did not want it to happen.
examples: I'm afraid I deleted your email **by accident**.

right.label: on purpose
right.text: The person wanted to do it; it was their intention.
examples: I'm sure she broke that vase **on purpose**; she never liked it.

lesson.heading: on + noun
rows: My boss is on the phone at the moment.
refusing to work because of a problem over pay or hours
where people can look at it
The books were on display in the window.
Part of the building was on fire.
on the train, boat or plane
Most of the passengers are now on board.
there for work, not a holiday
They're both in Germany on business.

lesson.heading: in + noun
rows: needing to do something very quickly
Why are they always in a hurry?
She won't make that mistake again in future.
The poor little girl was in tears.
in a moment / in a minute
I'll see you in a moment.

left.label: on time
left.text: Exactly at the right time, not late.
examples: Lessons begin at 8.30 and the students are usually here **on time**.
The meeting was planned for 11 am and we got there **on time**.

right.label: in time
right.text: Before the time when you need to be there.
examples: If we hurry, we'll be there **in time**.
Did you get to the cinema **in time** for the film?

lesson.heading: in the end or at the end?

left.label: in the end
left.text: Finally, after a lot of time or thought.
examples: We were tired of waiting, so **in the end** we went home.
It was a terrible journey, but we got there **in the end**.

right.label: at the end
right.text: In the last part of something.
examples: **At the end** of the book they get married.
He gets killed **at the end** of the film.

lesson.heading: up-to-date, out-of-date and at the moment
lesson.text: **Out-of-date** information is old and no longer correct. **Up-to-date** information is the most recent. **At the moment** means right now.

examples.text: I'm afraid this book's a bit **out-of-date**.
I try to keep **up-to-date** with all the changes.
I can't speak to you **at the moment**.

lesson.text: Say *I'm busy at the moment*, never ~~I'm busy in this moment~~.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition goes with each noun?
I'm afraid I deleted your email ___ accident.
exercises.explanation: By accident = you did not plan or want it to happen.
On purpose = the person wanted to do it.

exercises.prompt: I'm afraid I'm busy ___ the moment.
exercises.explanation: At the moment = right now. Never say in this moment.

exercises.prompt: I just saw them ___ chance - we hadn't planned to meet.
exercises.explanation: By chance = it wasn't planned; it was luck.

exercises.prompt: I saw smoke coming out of the window, and I realised the house was on ___.
Nobody is at the factory. The workers are all on ___.
exercises.explanation: On strike = refusing to work because of a problem over pay or hours.

exercises.prompt: These chocolates are expensive because they are all made by ___.
exercises.explanation: Made by hand = made without a machine.

exercises.prompt: I'm sorry I can't stop to talk now - I'm in a ___.
exercises.explanation: In a hurry = needing to do something very quickly.

exercises.prompt: She never thanked me for the present, so I won't buy her another one in ___.
I told them everything they wanted to know. I explained it all in ___.
exercises.explanation: In detail = including all the important information.

exercises.prompt: Match each meaning with the right prepositional phrase.

pairs.left: at exactly the right time, not late
before the time you need to be there
finally, after a lot of time
in the last part of a book or film
old, and the information is wrong
there for work, not a holiday

exercises.statement: 'I'm writing an email, but I'll be with you in a minute.' This means the speaker will come very soon.
exercises.explanation: Correct. In a minute / in a moment = not now, but very soon.
